F-01Must fixNEW — not on the checklist

"Mark all as read" wipes the edition with no way back

The double-check icon in the top bar marks every story read at once, with no confirmation. The full-screen "Fin." page then slides over everything, and the only way back, the Undo message, is hidden underneath it. The Daily, 390 and 884, day and night · #mr click www/index.html:11299 · finShow :7428 · #toast z-index 95 vs #fin z-index 2000

Why it matters
The first icon a curious new reader taps erases their first edition and shows a "Fin." screen with no visible undo.
The fix
Put the Undo message above the Fin page (one z-index line), and do not show Fin from mark-all when nothing was actually read; optionally ask "Mark 24 stories as read?" when more than a handful are affected.
Risk
Low for the stacking fix; medium for a confirmation box (tests click the button directly).
F-02Must fixNEW — not on the checklist

Back on the "Fin." page leaves the app

With the Fin page open, pressing Back (what the Android back button does inside the app) does not close it; the app is left instead. The reader, Settings and the side drawer all close correctly on Back because they register themselves as a layer; Fin does not. Fin page, any width · finShow www/index.html:7428 has no pushLayer('fin') · popstate handling :16161-16170

Why it matters
Being thrown out of the app right after finishing an edition feels like a crash.
The fix
Register Fin as a layer when it opens and close it on Back, copying the existing pattern used by the gallery and year-in-review pages.
Risk
Low; copies an existing pattern. Confirm on a phone (headless used history.back()).
F-03Must fixNEW — not on the checklist

Onboarding tells readers the swipe directions backwards

The last onboarding page says "Swipe a story right to save it, left to mark it read." The app does the opposite (right = mark read, left = save). The in-app tip that appears later states it correctly. Onboarding step 5, 390/884 · www/index.html:13402 · correct wording in TIPQ :12494

Why it matters
The very first instruction a new reader gets is wrong, so their first swipe does the opposite of what they meant.
The fix
Change the sentence to "Swipe a story right to mark it read, left to save it."
Risk
None (copy only).
R-01Must fixNEW — not on the checklist

An inline "Read more:" line cuts the rest of the story off, silently

When a story has a short "Read more: …" promo line in its middle (common on BBC, Guardian, Independent and WordPress sites), the cleaner treats that line as the end of the article and throws away everything after it. The chopped story is then counted as complete, so no "Partial story" label appears. Reader, all widths/modes · tidy rule 2 www/index.html:8932 (once 35% of the text has passed, any short line matching END ends the story) · END list :8767 includes "read more" · ENDMARK :9066 makes looksIncomplete say "complete"

Why it matters
The second half of ordinary news stories vanishes with no warning.
The fix
Only treat a short "end" line as the end when little text follows it (for example under a quarter of the story, or fewer than two real paragraphs); otherwise drop just that one line. This is a cleaning rule, not the fetch strategy, but it is extraction logic, so it is your call.
Risk
Medium: extraction heuristic; run the reader tests afterwards.
T-01Must fixNEW — not on the checklist

The Daily's photo cover never shows its photo

One day in three the Daily picks a photo cover when the lead story has a picture. The photo never appears on phone or Fold: the crop pass written for the other cover styles treats the full-bleed photo as the wrong shape, shrinks it to a small box and places it beneath the morning/evening artwork, so readers only ever see the artwork. The Daily › Today, 390 and 884, day/night, every theme · coverCrop www/index.html:6078 selector includes '#grid .dcov' · inset gets zIndex -1 at :6102/:6107 while the art SVG (.dcv-art, CSS :2974) paints over it · dayCoverHtml :15091

Why it matters
A whole cover treatment is dead: on the day the Daily promises a photo cover there is no photo.
The fix
Leave the Daily cover out of the crop pass (drop '#grid .dcov' from that selector) so it keeps its designed full-bleed photo. Then re-check Newsprint, where a bright photo makes the edition line hard to read: give it the normal shade gradient on photo covers.
Risk
Low-medium: the crop pass was written for the other cover styles; tests/cover_crop.js only covers those. Confirm on a phone.

R-02Should fixNEW — not on the checklist

Short but complete stories are labeled "Partial story"

A complete story of about 150-250 words that ends with a full stop is labeled "PARTIAL STORY — This may be only the start of the story." Anything under 400 words without an explicit end phrase gets the label. looksIncomplete www/index.html:9067 · flag set :9101 · label written :9667 · fixtures of 130/165/213/250 words all badged at 390 and 884

Why it matters
Wire briefs and notices are routinely 100-300 words; the badge cries wolf and readers stop believing it.
The fix
For a story's own page text of 120+ words, require a real sign of a cut (no final punctuation, an ellipsis, or a "read more / subscribe" tail) before labeling; keep the 400-word rule only for the behind-the-scenes rescue search.
Risk
Medium: the same flag drives the rescue search; soften only the label branch.
R-03Should fixNEW — not on the checklist

Share rows and raw markdown leak into story bodies

A share row shows as a line of underlined links ("Share on Facebook Tweet Email"), and raw markdown stays as typed: "## What the plan does", "* Adds three…", "[ ]" and "[x]" lines. tidy rule 1 www/index.html:8915-8925 only matches "share this" / "follow" · isolateExtras :8777 and junkClean :7004 do not normalize #, *, -, [ ]

Why it matters
Junk in the body is the fastest way to make a reader doubt the whole app.
The fix
Treat short link-only "share/tweet/email" lines as junk; turn "## " into a subheading, "* " into a bullet and drop "[ ]" markers in one pass over the paragraphs.
Risk
Low.
R-05Should fixNEW — not on the checklist

Web version: "Best available" voice never actually picks a voice

In a browser (not the Android app) the automatic voice choice never happens: it always falls back to the engine's default voice, possibly in another language or a remote one, even when a matching local voice exists. The check requires a quality score that only the Android voice list has. bestVoice www/index.html:10088 'if(!c.length||!c.some(v=>v.q))return null' · q only set by the plugin in loadVoices :10118 · voice/lang then unset at :9990 and :15578

Why it matters
Read-aloud on the web sounds worse than it needs to, or speaks in the wrong language.
The fix
Drop the quality-score requirement; rank by score, then default, then local; set the language from the browser when none is set.
Risk
Low. Android app unaffected.

Every other destructive control (Erase everything, Reset appearance, Remove a site, Reset this section, Clear history) asks first or offers Undo. This one acts on the tap. Settings › Downloads and Storage › Advanced · #clr click www/index.html:12436 · row :4882

S-05Should fixNEW — not on the checklist

Web version sends each background download to all four relays

On the web (not Android, which reads sites directly), every story pre-downloaded in the background is sent through all four public relays one after another, not just the first that works: 5 sites made 165 requests on one cold Daily load (40 stories × 4 routes). Cause: in background mode the winning route waits out a 6-second quiet gate before it reports success, while the 650ms stagger timer keeps launching the next relay. The privacy page says public relays are used only "if that fails", which is true for Android and for stories you open, not for this path. One story also contacted the Jina reader at the same instant as the first relay rather than as a fallback. fetchText1 www/index.html:5201-5255 (gate at :5236 before res(t) :5238; stagger in start() :5244) · getFull(a.link,true) from pump :9538 · bgGate :5131 · privacy.html lines 43 and 45

Why it matters
Each story address is handed to three outside services instead of one, and the browser does four times the network work.
The fix
When a usable body arrives, stop the stagger timer and abort the other routes before waiting on the quiet gate (a "won" flag the launcher checks).
Risk
Medium: shared fetch race; run the prefetch/relay tests.
S-08Should fixNEW — not on the checklist

Nothing says you are offline on a warm start

Open the app with stored stories and no connection: the Daily and All Stories show the stored stories as if fresh. No pill, no banner. The "Offline" pill next to the title exists but only for the user-chosen Offline mode, not for an actual lost connection. A cold start with no stored stories handles it well. body.offl #ttl::after www/index.html:678 · offApply :6146 · online/offline listeners :5841/:8221 never set a class

Why it matters
On a train with no signal the reader waits for new stories that cannot come and blames the sites.
The fix
On the browser's offline/online events (and at boot) toggle a second class that reuses the same pill.
Risk
Low.

"The Daily" in the top bar is cut at the bottom (content 28px tall in a 24px box with overflow hidden), at normal and large text sizes and at 884. .top h1 www/index.html:812 (#ttl)

Why it matters
A chopped letter on a magazine masthead looks like a bug.
The fix
A touch more line height or 3px of bottom padding.
Risk
Low (header 4px taller; check the docked tabs).
S-07Nice to haveNEW — not on the checklist

Add a site: the error message is far below the field

A non-address shows a clear message ("That doesn't look like a web address…") but 408px below the field, under the Starter packs / Near you / Browse topics cards. Screen readers hear it; sighted readers may not connect it to the field. #err in #dlg, 390 night · handler www/index.html:11283

Why it matters
The reader types again without seeing why it failed.
The fix
Move the message directly under the field's hint line.
Risk
Low.
S-09Nice to haveNEW — not on the checklist

"Reset this section" has no Undo; two spellings of offline

"Reset this section" asks for a second tap but offers no Undo, while "Reset appearance and reading settings" and the Quick setup presets do. Also "You are offline" (empty page) vs "You're offline" (messages). setReset www/index.html:10475 · empNoStories :12138

Why it matters
Consistency; a reset you did not mean is unrecoverable.
The fix
Snapshot the keys and offer Undo in the message, copied from the appearance reset; pick one spelling.
Risk
Low.
T-07Nice to haveNEW — not on the checklist

Sunrise/sunset card covers the hint message

The sunrise/sunset card that plays on a light/dark switch and the hint message share the bottom-left corner; the card covers the message's first words for about 4 seconds. .sky www/index.html:934 · #toast :1163

Why it matters
Minor, but the hint is unreadable exactly when it is shown.
The fix
Lift the sky card while a message is showing (one CSS rule).
Risk
Low.

  • All Stories is endless until truly empty (200 unique stories, honest end sentence); no duplicate stories across Daily/Headlines/All; "Next up · 4 stories" really has 4.

  • Search: relevant results, honest "No matches" with Clear.
  • Largest text size and a 22px root font: no overflow or clipping in bar, tabs, Daily, All, Brief, Headlines (single-column rules kick in).
  • Reader: Back/Escape return to the same card at the same offset; every ••• menu item present and labeled; Aa sheet (Large print, text size, Auto/Pages/Scroll) works; 25-word headline wraps without clipping; feed-only text after a 403 gets the correct Partial story note; duplicate captions, newsletter lines, author bios and related lists are removed; one-word lede gets no drop cap; the pre-built page turn is invisible by measurement (but see T-08).
  • Read-aloud: rate/pitch/prosody, sentence chunking, pause/resume position, late voice lists and the Android quality-scored voice pick are all sound; only the web voice pick (R-05) and the no-voices start (R-08) are off.
  • Night modes are designed, not inverted, in every live theme; no dark-on-dark card titles anywhere; badge plates tinted per theme in all six live themes; oled on a light phone falls back to Cypress day as designed; theme switch with a story open repaints correctly.
  • Cover styles Clean, Gazette, Magazine, Gallery, Index, Journal, Cinema, Type and the Daily paper/type/fallback covers at 390 and 884: no clipped headline with a 20-word title, no cut cover line, faces kept clear of text per the repo's own rule.
  • Settings: 13 settings stick after reload; presets Undo exactly; section resets touch only their own keys; destructive controls are 87-140px from frequent controls; Erase asks twice; Remove a site confirms.
  • Accessibility: no empty or duplicate icon-button names; no nested interactive elements; dialogs have role, focus-in and focus-return; Daily tabs arrow-key with roving tabindex; switches are role=switch; Light/Dark is a radiogroup; settings label contrast 6.9-11.4:1.
  • Offline/error copy in Manage your sites and the cold-start empty states is plain and correct; bad address and dead site in Add a site are handled well; empty Saved/History/Highlights/Stats pages are friendly.
  • Privacy: every outside service the app can contact (relays, rss2json, Jina, morss, Google/Bing News, Feedly search, GitHub updater, YouTube thumbnails, Google Fonts, jsDelivr font) is named on privacy.html; no analytics, tracker or beacon exists, so there is no toggle to honor; feeds are never fetched twice; Daily↔All switch makes 0 requests.

  • Performance: 60 sites / 528 stories and one site with 500 stories fling with no frame over 132ms; story open median 109ms; cold start median 484ms (headless, local server).
